name: gscode
description: IntelliSense for Call of Duty's GSC, CSC and GSH languages, across five games.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode, gscode.rawPath and gscode.modsPath are read from your user settings only, so an untrusted workspace cannot point the language server at other folders on disk.

virtualWorkspaces.description: The language server reads scripts from disk, so it needs a workspace on the local file system.

keybindings.when: editorTextFocus && (editorLangId == gsc || editorLangId == csc || editorLangId == gsh)

enumDescriptions: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare (2007)
Call of Duty: World at War (2008)
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009)
Call of Duty: Black Ops (2010)
Call of Duty: Black Ops III (2015)
gscode.game.description: Which Call of Duty game's GSC dialect this workspace targets. All five are verified against the game's own scripts. Only games with an implemented dialect are listed: naming any other resolves to Black Ops III, which used to happen silently and is now reported in the server log. If a file does not look like the selected game, the extension offers to switch.

gscode.raw.enabled.description: Master switch for reading the game's raw files. When disabled, gscode.rawPath and gscode.modsPath are ignored entirely and resolution uses the open workspace folders alone.

gscode.rawPath.description: Absolute path to the game's raw script folder. Set this when the folder you have open is a mod or a loose set of scripts, so its includes and path calls resolve against the game's own scripts. Left empty, the raw folder is looked for above the open workspace folders — so a mod inside the game install needs no setting at all — and if none is found, only those folders are indexed.

gscode.modsPath.description: Absolute path to the folder holding your mods, one subfolder per mod. A script inside a mod resolves against that mod first and the raw folder second, so a mod copy shadows the stock file it replaces.

enumDescriptions: Never warn when saving files inside a raw folder.
Warn only when saving stock scripts that shipped with the mod tools.
Warn when saving any file inside a protected raw folder.
gscode.rawFileWarningMode.description: When to warn about saving files inside the protected raw folder.

enumDescriptions: No background indexing; only open files are analyzed, and diagnostics that need to know about other files (missing/duplicate imports, unresolved calls) do not run.
Symbols, navigation, and references work across the workspace; cross-file diagnostics only for open files.
Partial, plus cross-file diagnostics for every indexed file, not just open ones.
gscode.workspaceIndexingMode.description: How much of the workspace (and game raw/mods folders) to index at startup.

gscode.enableWorkspaceCache.description: Persist analysed scripts to a per-workspace cache so cold starts restore unchanged files instead of re-parsing them.

enumDescriptions: Only files you have open.
Every indexed file of your own -- your mod and workspace folders, but not the stock scripts.
Everything indexed, including the game's stock scripts. Noisy, and you cannot edit them.
gscode.diagnostics.scope.description: Which files report problems. Files that are not open report the errors found when they were indexed; open files additionally get the cross-file lints.

gscode.outline.showAssignments.description: Show variable and field assignments as children of their function in the document outline.

gscode.codeLens.enabled.description: Show a 'N references' code lens above each function and class declaration.

gscode.inlayHints.parameterNames.description: Show parameter-name hints before arguments at call sites.

gscode.inlayHints.inferredTypes.description: Show inferred-type hints on local variable assignments.

gscode.inlayHints.macroParameterNames.description: Show macro parameter-name hints before the arguments of a #define invocation (e.g. IS_TRUE( __a: level.ready )). Off by default: macro parameters are named for the macro's body rather than for the caller.

gscode.completion.autoImport.description: Offer functions from scripts this file has not imported yet, adding the #using (or #include) line when one is accepted. Only after three characters have been typed, so the names already in scope come first.

gscode.completion.literals.description: Offer known strings, localized strings, and hash strings while typing inside a "..." / &"..." / #"..." literal (great for notify/waittill names).

enumDescriptions: Insert just the name.
Insert 'name()' with the cursor between the parentheses.
Also close a statement with a semicolon: 'name(<cursor>);'. Expressions such as 'x = f()' never gain one.
gscode.completion.callPunctuation.description: How much punctuation completing a function call brings with it.

gscode.completion.parameterHints.description: Show a function's parameter names inline in the suggestion list: 'get_players( team )' rather than 'get_players'. Filtering and insertion still use the name alone.

gscode.format.padParens.description: Pad the inside of control-flow and grouping parentheses: 'if ( x )' rather than 'if (x)'. Both appear in stock scripts, which are about 88% padded. Call parentheses have their own setting, gscode.format.padCallParens.

gscode.format.padCallParens.description: Pad the inside of call and declaration parentheses: 'foo( a, b )' rather than 'foo(a, b)'. Empty parentheses stay '()' either way. Turn this off and keep padParens on for the common 'if ( x )' with 'foo(x)' style.

gscode.format.padBrackets.description: Pad the inside of subscript and array-literal brackets: 'a[ i ]' rather than 'a[i]'. Function-pointer brackets '[[ ptr ]]' and empty '[]' stay tight either way. Stock scripts lean tight, about 4 to 1.

gscode.format.spaceBeforeControlParen.description: Put a space between a control-flow keyword and its parenthesis: 'if ( x )' rather than 'if( x )'. Applies to if, while, for, foreach and switch; 'return (' and 'case (' always keep their space. Independent of padParens, so 'if(x)', 'if( x )', 'if (x)' and 'if ( x )' are all reachable.

gscode.format.maxBlankLines.description: The longest run of blank lines the formatter preserves. Longer runs are collapsed to this many.

gscode.format.sortDirectives.description: Group and sort the directive block at the top of a file: #using, then #insert, then #namespace, then #define, then #precache, separated by blank lines. #using and #precache are sorted alphabetically; #insert and #define keep their relative order because they are order-sensitive. Applies to Format Document only, never to range or on-type formatting.

gscode.format.alignConsecutive.description: Align the operators of consecutive assignments so they line up in a column: a run of `a = 1;` statements at the same indentation is padded so every '=' sits in one column, one space past the longest left-hand side; a compound operator like '+=' puts its '=' in that column too. A blank line or a statement of a different kind ends a run; a comment on its own line does not. The same setting also aligns subscript and call-argument columns for same-shaped lines. Applies to all three formatting requests: format-on-type is limited to the run you are editing, Format Selection to the selection.

gscode.format.indentCaseLabels.description: Indent 'case' and 'default' labels one level inside their 'switch', with the statements under a label one level further. Off puts the labels in the switch's own column. Stock scripts indent them about 4 to 1.

gscode.format.indentDevBlocks.description: Indent the body of a '/# ... #/' dev block one level. Off keeps it at the level of the '/#', because a dev block is a compile-time switch rather than a scope. Stock scripts are split, about 3 flush to 2 indented.

gscode.format.alignMaxPadding.description: The most spaces consecutive alignment may add to one line. A line whose left-hand side is further than this from the rest of its run keeps a single space, and the rest still align; subscript and argument columns that would need more are left as written. 0 removes the limit.

gscode.format.fixCasing.description: Fix casing while formatting: keywords are lowercased ('isDefined' becomes 'isdefined'); a call takes the spelling of the function it resolves to ('getplayers()' becomes 'GetPlayers()', 'FOo()' becomes 'foo()' when the script declares 'function foo()'); namespaces take their #namespace spelling and classes their declaration's. A bare call resolves to a builtin before a script function of the same name; a qualified or threaded call means the script one. Macro names match exactly, so macros are never recased.

enumDescriptions: No server logging.
Errors only.
Warnings and errors.
General progress information (indexing, cache, lifecycle).
Detailed debug output, including per-request logging.
gscode.serverLogLevel.description: Verbosity of the GSCode language server's log output (the 'GSCode Server' channel). Applies live, no restart needed.

gscode.trace.server.description: Trace the LSP protocol traffic between VSCode and the GSCode language server.
